title: Context-Aware Request Casebook for Enterprise Data Controls (retention, redaction, exports)
creator: Rafael Gomez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit non-bug requests around logging redaction, retention policy changes, PII handling, and ad-hoc audit exports. Current intake is inconsistent across support, CSM, and SEs which causes slow SLAs, noisy engineering scopes, and missed compliance windows.

Goal: Design a context-aware casebook that standardizes intake fields, assigns an objective risk-and-effort score, and routes requests to the correct operator (Support runbook, SE-assisted project, Dedicated config, or Legal/Compliance lead) with clear SLOs and escalation paths. This should reduce TTR for high-risk governance work, prevent overloading engineering with low-risk operational asks, and enable auditability for enterprise customers.

Scope: initial MVP covers: retention window changes, log redaction requests (PII patterns + source logs), one-off audit exports (CSV/JSON), and requests to change access/audit trail retention. Excluded: new feature requests unrelated to controls, infra incident remediation (bug), or requests requiring third-party vendor action.

Approach overview:
1) Intake form (CSM/Support/Customer) with mandatory fields: request type, regulatory driver, requested time window, affected customers/data classes, export format, desired due date, and business justification.
2) Automated scoring engine (MVP rule-based) that outputs a 0-100 score across three axes: Regulatory Risk, Data Volume/Scope, Engineering Effort. Each axis is weighted; final score determines routing tier and SLO.
3) Contextual routing rules map score + request type to lanes: "Operational (Support)", "Config/Template (SE)", "Engineering Project", "Legal & Compliance Review".
4) Escalation playbook and required artifacts per lane (e.g., proof of authority, legal approval, signed NDA, test export sample).
5) Dashboard and audit trail: every routed request appends metadata and decision rationale for compliance reviews.

Deliverables: intake form template, scoring rubric, routing table, runbook per lane, dashboard mock for Console, communication scripts for customers, and a pilot with three enterprise accounts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Intake form implemented in Zendesk/HubSpot and available to CSM/Support with required validations.
2) Scoring engine (rule-based) returns a score and recommended lane for all sample requests in pilot dataset (>=95% deterministic mapping).
3) Routing table covers all prototyped scenarios and routes to one of four lanes.
4) Runbooks for each lane written and reviewed by Eng, Legal, and Support.
5) Pilot executed with 3 customers and average SLA for high-risk requests reduced from baseline by >=40%.
6) Audit trail persisted in Console with request metadata and final disposition.
7) Security/Legal sign-off on redaction export template.
8) Documentation and communication scripts reviewed and published to Confluence.
notes:
Scoring rubric prototype: Regulatory Risk (0-40): maps regulation type (GDPR/CCPA/SEC) and potential fines; Data Volume/Scope (0-35): estimated rows, log sources, and PII types; Engineering Effort (0-25): configuration only (low), SE-assisted (med), new infra work (high). Final score = sum.

Routing bands (example): 0-30 -> Operational (SLO: 7 business days), 31-60 -> SE/Config (SLO: 14 business days), 61-85 -> Engineering Project (SLO: 45 days + quarterly release window), 86-100 -> Legal Review + Exec approval (SLO: case-by-case).

Trade-offs discussed: rule-based scoring is faster for MVP but will generate edge-case false positives; will instrument for later ML reranking using historical closures. We also debated embedding workload cost estimation vs. simple effort bands—chose effort bands to keep intake friction low.

Engineering impacts: need a small API endpoint to accept intake payloads, a routing microservice (rule engine), and a lightweight persistence table in Console for audit metadata. Eng estimate: 8 points (ENG-1842 owner).

Compliance ask: Legal requires a template approval for exports containing PII and a mandatory attestation field on intake form.

Pilot selection: pick three customers spanning Hosted, Dedicated, and Private to validate routing differences and access constraints.
